audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL-focused specifications: EVM environment opcodes (Prague), block context instructions, transaction validation (EIP-3607), mining protocol (EIP-1571), and browser wallet account requests (EIP-1102).

out_of_scope: Mining Pool Protocol (EIP-1571 Stratum - external to EL core)

misclassified_entities.reason: Executing smart contracts are internal to the EVM execution environment, not external entities. They are the code being executed by the EL.
Historical block storage is internal EL state, not an external entity. Block hashes are retrieved from the node's own state database.
Threat actors are not external entities in a data flow trust model. EXT-ATTACKER represents a threat scenario, not a real data source interacting with the system.
EIP-1571 Stratum mining protocol is out of scope for EL core audit. Mining clients interact with pool servers, not directly with EL transaction/block processing.
Mining pool server is part of the EIP-1571 Stratum protocol, out of scope for EL core audit.
Generic protocol participant in EIP-1571 Stratum protocol, out of scope for EL core audit.

DApps interact with the browser wallet provider (EIP-1102), not directly with EL core. The wallet provider mediates. However, DApps do submit transactions via JSON-RPC, which is captured by EXT-RPC-CLIENT/EXT-TX-SUBMITTER.
Browser user interacting with wallet consent dialog is a client-side UX concern (EIP-1102), not an external entity interacting with EL core.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any entity can submit signed transactions via JSON-RPC. No authentication required. Transactions may have forged sender addresses (prevented by signature verification) or attempt to exploit validation gaps (e.g., EIP-3607 address collision). All transaction content must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P Protocol
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated and may propagate invalid blocks containing transactions from contract addresses (EIP-3607 violation) or other malformed data. All received blocks and transactions must be independently validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Client via eth_call/eth_estimateGas
trusted_external_entities.rationale: RPC simulation requests are unauthenticated. EIP-3607 sender code check is intentionally relaxed for simulations, but all other validation applies. Simulations must not modify state.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Validator) via Consensus
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block context values (coinbase, timestamp, prevrandao, gaslimit)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators set block context values that EVM instructions read (COINBASE, TIMESTAMP, PREVRANDAO, GASLIMIT). These are authenticated through consensus but individual values (especially PREVRANDAO) may be biasable by the proposer. Content validation by EL is limited to format checks; semantic correctness relies on consensus layer verification.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce check, sender CodeHash check (EIP-3607 - must equal EMPTYCODEHASH), gas limit validation, balance check. Transactions from addresses with deployed code must be rejected.

Full block validation required: all transactions must pass EIP-3607 sender code checks, standard transaction validation, state transition correctness. Blocks containing any invalid transaction must be rejected entirely.

Simulation requests must be read-only (no state modification). EIP-3607 sender code check may be bypassed for simulations. Input parameters must be validated for format correctness. Gas limits must be enforced to prevent resource exhaustion.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block header context (used by COINBASE, TIMESTAMP, NUMBER, PREVRANDAO, GASLIMIT, CHAINID opcodes)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block context values are set by the proposing validator and validated by consensus. EL must validate format (correct types, ranges) but relies on CL for semantic correctness. PREVRANDAO is biasable by proposers (1-bit bias). TIMESTAMP must be monotonically increasing. CHAINID must match configured network.
